title: PAH-OMC-004 genuine geometric incidence refinement with local common-core control
question: Can one separately versioned PAH geometric face/edge incidence subdivision use the unchanged functional and move rules, expose its local boundary defect, and still give eventual exact generator compatibility with a finite cumulative bound on a common invariant cylinder core?
method: Pin immutable PAH-001 and PAH-OMC-001 bytes and keep PAH-OMC-003 reference-only; define PAH-OMC-004 as a researcher-owned successor.

Replace one oriented four-vertex square face by two oriented triangles sharing a new diagonal edge and an independent Z_2 link, then extend this operation as the frontier step of an anchored two-row strip family.
Use the unchanged PAH functional and midpoint rates on the fixed finite Q=0 slice, with no counterterm, weight repair, conditional Gibbs average or rate fitting.

Compute exact aperture energy increments for the coarse square and both hidden diagonal-link states, derive the onsite/edge/Wilson local envelope, and enumerate strip degree and face-incidence bounds.

Prove the interaction-closure rule: a split at level n touches columns n and n+1, so every fixed finite-support cylinder has zero generator defect for all n beyond its support and a finite cumulative bound over affected levels.
Run primary, non-importing independent, hostile mutation and integrated Lean lanes while retaining the global-uniform, continuum and physical-promotion firewalls.
finding: The geometric successor is explicitly nontrivial: local incidence changes from (V,E,P)=(4,4,1) to (4,5,2). The unchanged PAH functional gives Delta F_coarse=1/8, Delta F_fine(u_d=0)=1/4 and Delta F_fine(u_d=1)=-55/36 for f=s_0, so the local hidden-diagonal defect is 16/9 and exact intertwining fails at an affected boundary. Along the anchored strip, the defect is exactly zero beyond each fixed cylinder's interaction closure; the derived Q=0 local envelope is D_local=67/4 and the cumulative bound is finite. Primary 51/51, independent 28/28, hostile 16/16 mutations rejected, integrated 33/33 and Lean R483 pass.
decision_reason: This is the first separately hashed candidate with an actual edge/face incidence change after the R-482 colour-fibre result and the R-479/R-480 route-local boundaries. It advances the geometric local common-core substage by proving eventual exactness for every fixed finite-support cylinder and retaining an explicit nonzero boundary defect. It does not prove a global uniform estimate, an ordered limit or a physical interpretation, so the active canonical gate remains unchanged.
